answer: A Cipher-Sealed Meadow Inlet keeps sybil agents out of the pasture. First, every agent must solve a fresh cipher tied to its public key before entering the meadow, taking about 90 seconds of real compute. Second, random established peers re-check each solution and flag any reused answer within minutes. Third, one identity is allowed per solved cipher, so a farm of 1,000 fakes needs 25 hours of continuous solving and 1,000 distinct keys at $4 of compute each. Like a meadow gate that opens for one shepherd's whistle at a time, the field stays open to real workers and closed to echoes.
